title: Grounded or silent: make every claim earn its place
brief: The retriever handed over three chunks and the model wrote five confident sentences. Which of them does the evidence support, and what should happen to the rest?

blocks.text: Three checks that sound alike and are not

blocks.caption: Answerability, groundedness and citation validity
head: Check
Question it asks
Runs
Typical signal
Catches
rows: Does the evidence contain an answer at all?
Reranker score cutoff, a retrieval evaluator such as CRAG [[r25]], an answerability instruction
Confident answers built on weak retrieval
Is each claim entailed by the evidence?
NLI model, LLM judge, Azure groundedness detection [[r4]]
Does each cited span exist and support the claim?
Id and span lookup plus entailment on that span

blocks.title: Ways to enforce grounding
blocks.intro: Pick by the cost of a wrong answer, the document length and the language. Each one also adds tokens or latency.

options.name: Instruction only
options.summary: Tell the model to answer from the sources, to cite, and that it may say it does not know.
pros: Anthropic guidance recommends explicit permission to say I don't know [[r23]]
cons: Not a guarantee, because the model can still over-claim
options.bestWhen: Low risk, or as the first layer under stronger checks.
options.avoidWhen: It is the only control in a regulated setting.

options.name: Quote first, then answer
options.summary: For long documents, ask for word-for-word quotes before the answer.
pros: Anthropic suggests it for documents over 20k tokens
Makes the evidence visible and checkable
cons: A second step adds latency and tokens
Quotes can be correct and misused
options.bestWhen: Long source documents and a need to audit the evidence.
options.avoidWhen: Latency is tight and sources are short.

options.name: NLI or judge faithfulness check
options.summary: Check every claim against its evidence with an entailment model or a prompted LLM.
pros: SummaC scores sentence-level NLI and aggregates it [[r19]]
AlignScore is a unified alignment function trained on many tasks [[r21]]
TRUE meta-evaluates factual consistency metrics across tasks, which helps you pick one [[r20]]
NeMo's `self check facts` rail scores 0.0 to 1.0 against `$relevant_chunks` [[r14]]
cons: A judge that shares the generator's blind spots misses the same errors
Quality depends on the model following the check prompt
options.bestWhen: Claims carry real cost and you can run a second pass.
options.avoidWhen: You stream tokens and cannot hold the answer.

options.name: Azure groundedness detection
options.summary: A Content Safety API that checks an answer against supplied grounding sources and can optionally correct it.
pros: Non-reasoning mode returns a fast verdict, reasoning mode explains ungrounded segments
cons: In Foundry guardrails it applies to models, not agents
options.bestWhen: English content on Azure, and a managed claim check is acceptable.
options.avoidWhen: Content is mostly non-English, or the agent surface is the target.

meta.v: 55,000 characters of sources, 7,500 characters of text plus query, query of 3 words or more

options.name: Retrieval-confidence abstention
options.summary: Do not generate when the evidence is weak.
pros: Pairs with a reranker score cutoff or a CRAG-style evaluator
cons: Does not check the claims in an answer that was generated
Cutoffs drift when scoring models update
options.bestWhen: Many questions are unanswerable and a refusal is acceptable.
options.avoidWhen: Used as the only grounding control.

steps.md: Is the question answerable from the evidence?

blocks.title: Pricing a cutoff
blocks.expr: cost per query = P(wrong answer shipped) x C_wrong + P(false abstention) x C_abstain

vars.v: share of answers that are wrong and reach the user
share of answerable questions the system refuses
your cost for each error, in any consistent unit

blocks.example: Raising a cutoff cuts wrong answers from 4% to 1.5% and raises false abstentions from 3% to 9%. With C_wrong = 20 and C_abstain = 2, cost per query falls from 0.04 x 20 + 0.03 x 2 = **0.86** to 0.015 x 20 + 0.09 x 2 = **0.48**. A cheaper wrong answer flips this.

items.symptom: Citations resolve and the claim is still wrong.
items.cause: Citation validity checks that a source exists, not that it supports the claim.
items.fix: Add a claim-level entailment check against the cited span, and sample it with human review.

items.symptom: Groundedness verdicts look odd on non-English answers.
items.cause: Azure groundedness detection is optimised for English and does not reject other languages.
items.fix: Calibrate a judge or NLI model per language, and test each language slice.

items.cause: The cutoff or answerability prompt is too tight.
items.fix: Build a labelled set of answerable and unanswerable questions and track false abstentions next to wrong answers.

items.symptom: Every answer is blocked after switching to a reasoning model.
items.cause: NeMo's `self check facts` fails closed with score 0.0 when the model spends its `max_tokens` before answering.
items.fix: Raise the token budget or use a non-reasoning model for the check.

items.symptom: Requests with citations on and a JSON schema return HTTP 400.
items.cause: Anthropic citations are incompatible with structured outputs.
items.fix: Choose one, or add the citations in a second step.

blocks.title: A citation is provenance, not proof
blocks.md: A reference tells the reader where text came from. It does not show that the sentence follows from it. ALCE benchmarks answers with citations [[r22]], and the guardrail is a separate check that compares claim and span.

quiz.q: A cutoff change lowers wrong answers from 5% to 2% and raises false abstentions from 4% to 10%. With C_wrong = 25 and C_abstain = 3, what is the expected cost per query after the change?
quiz.explain: After the change the cost is 0.02 x 25 + 0.10 x 3 = 0.5 + 0.3 = 0.8. Before it was 0.05 x 25 + 0.04 x 3 = 1.37, so the change is worth it at these costs. If C_wrong were close to C_abstain, the extra refusals would outweigh the saved errors.

quiz.q: This check log shows a passing citation and a wrong claim. Which control is missing?

code.code:
claim:       Refunds are accepted within 60 days [2]
cited span:  Refunds are accepted within 30 days of delivery.
id [2] in retrieved set: pass

options: Lower the temperature so that the model copies the source more closely
Add a claim-level entailment check against the cited span
Increase k so that more chunks can be cited for each claim
Validate that every cited id exists in the retrieved set
quiz.explain: The id check already passes, so it cannot be the missing control. The claim contradicts the span, which only an entailment check on the claim and its span detects. Temperature and k change what the model sees or how random it is, not whether a claim is checked.

quiz.q: Select every true statement about Azure groundedness detection as of 2026-10-13.
options: Accuracy is optimised for English, although the API does not reject other languages
Reasoning mode explains ungrounded segments and non-reasoning mode returns a fast verdict
In Foundry guardrails the groundedness control also applies to agents
It is generally available in every Azure region
quiz.explain: The docs describe both language behaviour and the two modes. The Foundry overview says previews such as groundedness are not yet supported for agents, so a control on an agent does not take effect. The feature is labelled preview and is available only in specific regions.

quiz.q: Put the steps of a grounded answer pipeline in order.
items: Gate on evidence: is the question answerable?
Generate with quote-first or native citations
Validate that cited ids and spans exist
quiz.explain: Gate first so you spend no generation on unanswerable questions. Citation ids are cheap to validate before the costlier entailment pass. The response decision comes last because it needs every verdict.

takeaways: Answerability, groundedness and citation validity are three different checks
A citation proves provenance, not entailment
Price the cutoff: wrong answers and false abstentions both cost something
Azure groundedness detection is preview, English-optimised and limited by region as of 2026-10-13
